results.name: Need some space?
results.description:
This model is the result of further programming experiments (C++) on my path to recreating space objects. 

If you're curious, here are a few clues about its creation :

* I initially scattered the stars in a disk-like fashion, and gave them a tangential initial rotation speed.
* The system is driven through a mix of gravitational forces and vorticity, but I had to create additional attractors in a rotating spiral pattern to emphasize the shape of the galaxy arms.
* Note that this "simulation" does not take into consideration the reciprocical attraction between stars (that would take way too long for now...).
* Computing 150 iterations for 50k particles and 54 forces (most due to the "spiral forcing")  took approximately 20 seconds on my laptop. 
* Each particle was colored in a range related to their initial distance to the center of the galaxy (red-ish in the center, blue-ish at the rim).

And [here](https://skfb.ly/6JBWp) is an animated example of the iterative process !

results.name: Ship in a bottle
results.description:
**CC-Attribution-NonCommercial** Based on a scan of a replica of the "Mayflower" ship, processed by @spogna and available [here](https://skfb.ly/6u8T6). Like in the [Mosquito in Amber](https://skfb.ly/6xWCO), most of my attention was spent on normal maps, roughness and refraction settings to try to make this model as realistic as possible. I actually had to create a secondary internal surface for the bottle, and also relied on clear coat options for the glass material in order to try to give the model a feeling of thickness. To try to get the opacity right, I used refraction on the outer layer (normals offset checked), and alpha-blending on the inner one. All of the modeling was done with Blender, but the critical part for the model aesthetics relies on Sketchfab materials and post-processing.
> > Another ship in a bottle > > Has got no place to sail > > To see the waves getting darker every hour > > The stars have lost their power > > In the sky >
**Beck**, *Ship in a bottle*.

results.name: DreadRoamer
results.description:
Dreadroamers are highly xenophobic, filthy creatures who travel the stars in stolen fleets, attacking and murdering wherever they encounter life. Their pirate fleet usually consists of a variety of rag-tag vessels that have been captured from the other races. These vessels tend to be in poor condition and have often been overly-modified to suit the orc-like dreadroamer’s taste.

They are a violent, ugly species whose physical appearance varies quite a bit. They tend to be hideous, troll-like and non-symmetrical, and have cybernetically modified their bodies for war. Such is the nature of their biology that dismembered limbs will grow back through-and-around existing impediments in a matter of days. They commonly use this ability to graft weapons and gear to their (vaguely humanoid) forms.

results.name: The Upper Vestibule
results.description:
**Welcome to [The Hallwyl Museum](https://goo.gl/qbZSY4) in Stockholm, Sweden.**

Once the home of [Walther](https://goo.gl/79nUeT) and [Wilhelmina von Hallwyl](https://goo.gl/Y8iiJs).

The Vestibule was the main entrance where both the Hallwyls and their guests entered the house. When you walk up the stairs you will see portraits of mainly Walther von Hallwyl´s ancestors. 

The portraits here date from the 16th to the 19th century. Walther and Wilhelmina inherited the portraits along with the family's main seat, the medieval castle [Schloss Hallwil](https://goo.gl/dsWmoe) in Switzerland. 

As they wanted to leave the castle with all its furnishings intact the ancestral portraits were copied by the artist [Julius Kronberg](https://goo.gl/PS1hEg). The originals were sent back to Switzerland when the Stockholm house was bequeathed to the Swedish state. 

![](https://i.imgur.com/mAilg0r.jpg)

The images for this project were captured using an [array](https://goo.gl/ePHjDr) of four Panasonic Lumix GX8 cameras.

results.name: Of Planes and Satellites
results.description:
2200 satellites orbits and 67000 flight routes visualized in 3D 🛰️✈️ ! ### Info * Orbits are correctly scaled. * Maximum airplanes altitude is overly exaggerated (by a factor of ~300). * I'd advice you to visit the [Europen Space Agency (ESA) website](https://www.esa.int/Enabling_Support/Space_Transportation/Types_of_orbits) to understand the different types of orbits, and learn why the ISS orbits around Earth in ~1h40 or why your satellite dish needs to be precisely calibrated. ### Orbits categories * Dark blue: Communications * Light blue: Earth Observation (optical, radar, meteo...) * Red/Orange: Positioning systems (GPS, Galileo, BeiDou...) * Green: R&D and Space science ### Resources * Orbits: https://www.ucsusa.org/resources/satellite-database * Airports and routes: https://github.com/jpatokal/openflights/ * Landmask/borders: http://www.shadedrelief.com/natural3/pages/extra.html
**Note:** Randomizing orbits Z-rotation (more realistic) looks like: ![](https://i.imgur.com/KSQTqVK.jpg)

results.name: Galactic Incident
results.description:
I tried to simulate a galaxy with particle systems in C++ (using the reciprocical attraction between stars this time, which my [previous "static" test](https://skfb.ly/6JyVO) did not take into account), but a minor coding error resulted in the creation of a miniature rogue black hole in it... 

AAaaaaahhh, the joys of programming !

The animation still ended up looking fabulous, and although the download is quite heavy *( approximately 50k particles x 60 steps = 3M vertices )*, it seems to run very smoothly once loaded !
